items.title: Can Liquid Biopsy Predict the Future of a Tumour? A Critical Review of AI-Enabled Longitudinal Modelling for Cancer Evolution and Treatment Resistance
items.abstract: Cancer behaves as a dynamic evolutionary system, whereas conventional tissue biopsy and imaging provide incomplete temporal information about how a tumour is changing. This review critically examines whether longitudinal liquid-biopsy measurement, combined with artificial intelligence (AI), can move oncology from tumour monitoring toward genuine prediction of cancer evolution and treatment resistance. We synthesise mechanistic, clinical, and computational evidence on circulating tumour DNA, circulating tumour cells, extracellular vesicles, and multimodal liquid-biopsy platforms, together with AI approaches applied to longitudinal cancer data, drawing on landmark and recent studies across colorectal, lung, breast, and ovarian cancer. Current evidence distinguishes three increasingly demanding tasks: early detection, longitudinal monitoring, and genuine forecasting. Longitudinal circulating tumour DNA analysis can detect molecular progression and emerging resistance mutations months before radiographic progression, and machine-learning models can stratify survival using serial biomarker metrics; however, most published "AI prediction" studies demonstrate earlier detection or prognostic association rather than prospectively validated forecasting of a future, patient-specific event. Biological variability in tumour shedding, analytical noise, small and irregularly sampled longitudinal datasets, overfitting, data leakage, weak external validation, and limited interpretability constrain the transition from detection to actionable prediction. AI-enabled liquid biopsy has genuine potential to forecast tumour trajectories, but current evidence is considerably stronger for molecular monitoring and early detection than for prospectively validated, clinically actionable prediction. Realising this potential will require standardised assays, prospective longitudinal cohorts with predefined prediction horizons, rigorous external and temporal validation, calibrated and interpretable models, and interventional trials linking predictions to treatment decisions before AI-enabled liquid biopsy can be considered ready to guide clinical care.

items.title: Case studies on the use of AI in precision medicine and targeted therapies
items.abstract: The implementation of technology application of artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare transformed the thinking of the one-size-fits-all method of healthcare; it has brought about a new world of scientific developments and personalized medicine. Diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of patients can be prescribed individually by applying AI, which could be achieved with the help of applying big data analytics, genomics, and machine learning algorithms. This paradigm becomes more accurate in the diagnosis, maximization of the therapeutic interventions, and the overall clinical outcome. The AI models can analyze complex biological trends, predict a danger of illnesses, and help clinicians make evidence-based treatment decisions. Despite stunning advancements, AI still has some limitations concerning moral self-governing, data security, discrimination, and adherence to the rules. The future of AI in personalized healthcare is to formulate explainable models, create interdisciplinary partnerships, and give fair access to the world over the populations. This chapter talks about the future trend of AI-based personalized healthcare, the potential of transformative possibilities, what it can be used in, its weaknesses, and future implications. It indicates how the human intuition and the AI intelligent capability may be used together to create a sustainable, inclusive, and patient-centered healthcare setting.

items.title: Challenges and Benefits of Implementing Smart Hospital Systems in Specialized Orthopedic Centers: A Systematic Review
items.abstract: The increasing complexity of healthcare services has encouraged specialized orthopedic centers to adopt smart hospital systems as an approach to improve service integration, operational efficiency, and patient-centered care. However, the implementation of these systems remains challenging due to technological, organizational, financial, and human resource limitations. This study aims to explore the benefits and challenges of implementing smart hospital systems in specialized orthopedic centers by examining their contributions to healthcare performance, operational processes, and patient experience. This research employed a systematic literature review approach by analyzing relevant studies related to smart hospitals, digital transformation, artificial intelligence, hospital information systems, and orthopedic healthcare services. A total of 25 studies were selected through a PRISMA-based screening process from an initial 200 identified records. The findings indicate that smart hospital systems provide significant benefits, including improved workflow coordination, faster access to medical information, enhanced clinical decision-making, increased surgical precision through advanced technologies, and improved continuity of rehabilitation care. Nevertheless, several challenges were identified, including limited infrastructure, high implementation costs, interoperability issues, data reliability concerns, and the need for user adaptation and training. In conclusion, smart hospital systems support more efficient, integrated, and patient-oriented orthopedic healthcare services; however, successful implementation requires technological readiness, organizational commitment, and continuous improvement strategies.

items.title: CHATGPT IN THE ETHNOMATHEMATICS ACTIVITY DESIGN PROCESS: PRE-SERVICE MATHEMATICS TEACHERS’ PERSPECTIVES
items.abstract: This study explored the effectiveness of ChatGPT in designing ethnomathematics activities based on pre-service mathematics teachers’ experiences, considering the benefits and challenges faced by pre-service teachers during the ethnomathematics task design process using ChatGPT. The participants were 37 senior pre-service mathematics teachers enrolled in elementary mathematics teacher education program at a public university. Data were gathered using a pre-information form assessing participants' prior knowledge of artificial intelligence tools, the activity design process, and ethnomathematics concept, as well as an opinionform to elicit their views on using ChatGPT for task design. The qualitative data were analyzed through content analysis of the participants' written responses on both forms. The findings indicated that all participants had sufficient prior knowledge of artificial intelligence tools and the activity design process, whereas their prior knowledge of ethnomathematics was limited. The findings highlight the benefits of using ChatGPT in activity design process, such as time efficiency and creative idea generation, as well as the challenges, including some pedagogical and technical limitations. These results emphasize that ChatGPT should be seen as a supportive tool rather than as a substitute for teachers’ skills and knowledge.

items.title: Clinical evaluation of AI Chatbots’ performance and safety for total parenteral nutrition planning in critically ill patients: a simulation-based benchmarking study
items.abstract: Introduction Total parenteral nutrition (TPN) is essential for critically ill adults unable to meet their nutritional needs via the gastrointestinal tract. Recent advancements in large language models (LLMs) have sparked interest in their potential to support healthcare providers in complex clinical decisions. Nonetheless, no prior research has systematically compared publicly accessible chatbots to pharmacist-developed reference TPN plans across a diverse patient cohort, using a predefined, guideline-based rubric assessing accuracy, completeness, safety, error types, and numerical precision. This study presents a simulation-based benchmarking to evaluate (i) the accuracy and comprehensiveness of chatbot-generated TPN plans, (ii) their safety, acceptability, and error profiles, and (iii) the numerical agreement and concordance with expert pharmacist references. Methods This benchmarking study, based on simulations and cross-sectional analysis, evaluated the performance of four publicly accessible AI chatbots—ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, and Perplexity—in formulating TPN plans for critically ill adults. Copilot declined to generate patient-specific TPN plans; this refusal was retained as a performance outcome, while Copilot was excluded from analyses requiring an analyzable TPN prescription. Each chatbot produced one plan for each of 10 standardized clinical cases, resulting in a total of 30 TPN plans. Friedman tests, Kendall’s W , and Holm-adjusted Wilcoxon signed-rank tests were used for comparative analyses. Results ChatGPT produced comprehensive plans for all 10 cases, compared to 6 plans from Gemini and 4 from Perplexity. The median accuracy was 57.7% for ChatGPT, 43.9% for Gemini, and 38.5% for Perplexity, with no statistically significant overall difference ( p = 0.124). However, ChatGPT performed better than Perplexity in pairwise comparison (adjusted p = 0.035). There was a significant difference in completeness among the chatbots ( p = 0.003; Kendall’s W = 0.57), with median scores of 64.6, 41.9, and 32.3%, respectively. All 30 plans had at least one major or critical safety issue, 7 (23.3%) contained a critical concern, and 19 (63.3%) were rejected. The most common errors were related to electrolytes (90.0%), micronutrients (70.0%), and monitoring (66.7%). Recommendations from chatbots often exceeded pharmacist-derived values, with median relative differences of +47% for energy, +120% for lipids, and +100% for potassium. Bland–Altman analysis revealed considerable variability in the agreement. Conclusion ChatGPT produced the most comprehensive TPN plans among chatbots. However, none showed enough accuracy, safety, or concordance for independent use. All plans had critical issues, especially with electrolytes, micronutrients, monitoring, and refeeding precautions. AI chatbots can support education or planning but require review by a well-trained clinician before clinical use.

items.title: CNN-Based Detection of Schizophrenia using EEG Data
items.abstract: To explore the potential for timely diagnostic and cure of mental disorders utilizing the Artificial intelligence (AI) it is necessary to examine its impact. This chapter explores the role of Convolution Neural Networks for the detection of Schizophrenia (SZ) by using the Electroencephalograms (EEG). EEG constitutes the physiological signals recorded from a specific area. AI techniques leveraging the Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) have presented remarkable outcomes in mental health issues diagnosis. The use of CNN in line with high dimensional data had paved the way for exploring impacting signs of mental disorders like depression, schizophrenia and autism. EEG data signals formulate the fundamental ally in capturing autonomic responses and neurophysiological related with these ailments. Here in this chapter, we present the role of CNN for detecting schizophrenia by using EEG data. As Schizophrenia is a state of mental illness that led to behavioural disparities, confused speech and illusions all of which have been widely examined using EEG data because of its non-invasive nature and high temporal purpose. Most of the previous studies have examined the full channel EEG data available or by using composite feature selection approach for the relevant feature mining, leading to high data processing and data redundancy. In our case we have organised an approach to overcome the full channel dependence of EEG data for detection of SZ by only taking in the account subset of regional channels. The EEG data experimented in this work is publically available and is presented by the Association of Psychiatry & Neurology in Warsaw, Poland. A channel selection framework has been proposed that measures the importance of various EEG channels across various brain regions, which is followed by training of a CNN-based classification model. The experimentation result obtained provided us the three key region centric EEG channels that are ‘Cz, T3 and T4’, using this regional subset the accuracy of classification is 67.79%, which is more that full channel data (63.35%). The enhanced regional method attained sensitivity (61.11%) and specificity (71.86%), emphasizing that the prior selection of channel improves the disease identification accuracy and brings down the computational overheads. The outcomes presented in this chapter pinpoints the influence of using CNN with regional subset channel EED data for schizophrenia detection, furthermore, we have also emphasised the challenges and ethical considerations surrounding data privacy.

items.title: Co‐Discovery of Workforce Wellness: Flourishing Through Aesthetic Engagement in a Canadian Healthcare Organization
items.abstract: Healthcare systems continue to face significant workforce challenges that threaten staff well-being, retention, and quality of care. Workforce wellness is increasingly recognized as essential to sustaining a stable and engaged healthcare workforce, yet it is frequently addressed as an individual concern rather than as an organizational, relational, and system-level phenomenon. A qualitative descriptive design with complementary arts-informed engagement examined how staff experience workforce wellness and how organizational environments shape well-being within a Canadian healthcare organization. The final analytic sample included 13 staff members representing diverse organizational roles. Participants submitted a written narrative and a self-chosen aesthetic expression representing what wellness at work meant to them. Written narratives were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis, while aesthetic expressions functioned as reflective prompts and knowledge-sharing outputs rather than formal analytic data. Six interconnected themes were identified: psychological safety in a connected community, empowerment through creative expression, culturally inclusive wellness, holistic work-life balance, flexible and supportive environments, and active growth. Together, the themes position workforce wellness as a relational, emotional, and collective phenomenon shaped by leadership practices, organizational culture, and enabling systems, conceptualized as an integrated workforce wellness ecosystem. Findings translate staff experiences into system-level opportunities, including psychological safety practices, flexible work design, culturally inclusive supports, creative engagement, protected recovery, and growth-oriented leadership. Co-design with the organization's Wellness Committee and EDI Council ensured the research asked and addressed questions meaningful to knowledge users.

items.title: Collaborative Learning and Social Learning in Augmented Reality, Virtual Reality, and Metaverse Environments: A Scoping Review
items.abstract: Collaborative and social learning are increasingly supported by extended reality (XR) technologies, that is, augmented reality (AR), virtual reality (VR), and mixed reality (MR) and the metaverse. However, their potential to support broader social learning processes beyond structured collaboration remains underexplored. This scoping review examines how XR and the metaverse support collaborative learning and social learning and looks into cooperative learning, group learning, and peer learning, identifying their educational benefits, challenges, and research gaps. In total, 213 studies from ACM, IEEE, Scopus, and Web of Science were analyzed to address six research questions. Specifically, the study examines relevant review and experimental studies to synthesize evidence from both primary and secondary research. The findings indicate seven main topics discussed within the literature and reveal a growing research field increasingly emphasizing pedagogical and social dimensions, yet predominantly focused on collaborative learning (89.7%) rather than social learning (10.3%). The existing literature indicates improvements in engagement, motivation, collaboration, communication, and learning achievement, while studies that focused on social learning, which primarily employed VR in higher education, additionally highlight improvements in self-efficacy, critical thinking, and social skills. However, technological limitations, accessibility concerns, lack of training and educational resources, implementation costs, and insufficient pedagogical guidance remain significant challenges. Short-term interventions and limited theoretical grounding further constrain the understanding of sustained social learning processes. The findings highlight the need for longitudinal and theoretically grounded research to better understand observational learning, community participation, and identity development in immersive environments. Finally, it highlights generative artificial intelligence (AI)-driven avatars as emerging social agents that merit attention in future social learning and social-emotional learning research.

items.title: Common Sense and Rationality
items.abstract: Abstract Common sense and rationality are two of the fundamental notions in philosophy that define human thinking, reasoning, and behavior. In general, common sense denotes the practical knowledge and beliefs possessed by ordinary people, while rationality implies logical thinking and justified reasoning. Philosophers of all times – from Aristotle to Thomas Reid, fromDescartes to Hume, from Kant to Moore and Ludwig Wittgenstein – have explored the relations between common sense and rationalityin their own ways. This investigation discusses the question about how common sense and rationality are associated in philosophy. The study also argues that common sense is the base of human knowledge and thinking, which is corrected by the notion of rationality. Moreover, this work will explore the importance of common sense for ethics, science, education, politics, and modern technology-based society. For many years, common sense has been a prominent element of philosophical research, representing the basis of human reasoning, but being criticized by sceptics and rationalists. From Aristotle and Thomas Reid up to the contemporary discussions about artificial intelligence, common sense continues to be an important notion in terms of understanding human knowledge, ethics, politics, science, and education.Six related issues to be explored in this essay include common sense and skepticism; ethics and political rationality; common sense in science, education, and political philosophy; artificial intelligence and common sense reasoning; and modern philosophical discussions on common sense and rationality. Philosophical analysis in this study shows that common sense cannot be taken as an infallible source of knowledge, nor can it be viewed as merely a prejudice. Instead, it is a type of rationality used by humans in practice. Keywords: Common Sense, Rationality, Practical Wisdom, Skepticism, Philosophy, Ethics, Judgment, Artificial Intelligence, Science

items.title: Comparing language models and machine learning classifiers for detecting humorous vaccine misinformation on social media
items.abstract: Abstract Misinformation embedded in humor on social media can be difficult to detect and mitigate. This study investigates the effectiveness of traditional machine learning (ML) models, pre-trained neural language models, and large language models (LLMs) in identifying humor-laden misinformation related to COVID-19 vaccines on Twitter. A dataset of 1,500 tweets was randomly sampled from a corpus of 17,945 humorous vaccination disclosures, with human coders annotating the presence of misinformation. We compared logistic regression, a linear support vector classifier (SVC), RoBERTa, and OpenAI’s GPT-4o with a zero-shot and a few-shot prompt, together with a keyword baseline. The few-shot GPT-4o prompt had the highest mean recall and F1 score for the types of misinformation indicated in the prompt and had higher recall and F1 than a keyword baseline built from those same terms. RoBERTa’s accuracy, precision, and F1 score did not differ significantly from GPT-4o’s, and its performance changed little with smaller training sets. Logistic regression and SVC showed lower accuracy, recall, and F1 scores than RoBERTa and the few-shot GPT-4o prompt. This study underscores the potential of LLMs to augment human efforts in detecting complex forms of misinformation on social media and highlights the importance of model selection based on task requirements.

items.title: Contradictions and Challenges in the New Era
items.abstract: The new academic wave is examined here not as a smooth process of modernisation but as a field of productive tension. Drawing on the concept of dilemmatic space , the analysis treats contradiction as a structural feature of meaningful institutional change rather than a sign of poor implementation. Such tensions cannot be resolved once and for all; they must be continually negotiated. The discussion traces several interconnected areas of tension. Ethical concerns emerge where artificial intelligence (AI) adoption, datafication, and digital surveillance advance more rapidly than the governance frameworks needed to regulate them, raising questions of academic integrity, algorithmic opacity, and unequal levels of AI literacy. At the same time, digital transformation frequently reproduces – and in some cases intensifies – existing inequalities related to income, geography, disability, gender, and academic precarity, challenging assumptions that digitalisation is inherently democratic. Further tensions arise between the pressure to innovate and the slower rhythms of academic autonomy, collegiality, and deliberation, with technocentrism, curriculum marketisation, and change fatigue appearing as recurring manifestations of this friction. Resistance to digital transformation is therefore interpreted not as an obstacle to be overcome but as a source of insight into the limitations and unintended consequences of reform. Concerns about institutional autonomy add another layer of complexity, as growing dependence on digital platforms, questions of data sovereignty, and political pressures on academic freedom increasingly shape the conditions under which universities operate. The chapter proposes an integrated governance framework grounded in six principles: ethics should guide deployment, equity should be embedded by design, wellbeing should be recognised as a condition of sustainable transformation, resistance should be treated as a form of institutional learning, educational purpose should shape technological choices, and institutional autonomy should be actively protected.

In response to systemic corruption, clientelism, and the obsolescence of traditional powers (legislative, executive, judicial, municipal, and partisan), an unappealable transition towards direct participation is proposed. items.title: Cyber-physical protection of microprocessor architectures of railway automation against deliberate electromagnetic interferences of high power
items.abstract: This paper presents the development of a cyber-physical protection system for railway microprocessor automation architectures against intentional high-power electromagnetic interference. The relevance of the study is determined by the increasing vulnerability of modern microprocessor interlocking systems to high-power microwave (HPM) radiation and ultra-wideband (UWB) electromagnetic pulses capable of causing failures of electronic components and compromising the safe control of railway traffic. The objective of the research is to develop an intelligent protection architecture that integrates structural electromagnetic shielding with an Edge Artificial Intelligence (Edge AI) module for rapid detection of hazardous electromagnetic events and initiation of protective actions. Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) is employed to process transient electromagnetic signals and generate phase-invariant spectrograms, while their classification is performed using a lightweight MobileNet convolutional neural network optimized for deployment on an STM32H7 microcontroller. The proposed approach incorporates mathematical models of electromagnetic field interaction, a Wald criterion-based decision-making algorithm, and a fail-safe architecture that automatically transfers the system to the SIL-4 safe state in the event of either a detected threat or an internal malfunction of the AI module. Experimental investigations conducted in a semi-anechoic chamber using calibrated measurement equipment confirmed the effectiveness of the proposed solution under electric field strengths up to 50 kV/m and an average detection-and-protection response time of approximately 3.1 ms. The scientific novelty of the research lies in the integrated application of spectral signal analysis, Edge AI technologies, and functional safety principles for protecting critical railway infrastructure against intentional electromagnetic attacks. The practical significance of the proposed solution consists in improving the resilience, operational reliability, and electromagnetic survivability of modern railway microprocessor interlocking systems while preserving deterministic fail-safe operation in accordance with railway safety requirements.

items.title: Cybernetic resilience in human–AI crisis response networks: a theory of adaptive emergence with empirical validation framework
items.abstract: Purpose This research addresses the following specific theoretical deficiency: while existing resilience frameworks do indeed consider the process of recovery or adaptation of crisis systems at the level of individuals, they fail to explain the ways in which human–artificial intelligence (AI) hybrid networks create emergent adaptive capacities not held by humans or AI alone. We develop the concept of cybernetic resilience to explain this emergent property. Design/methodology/approach This conceptual theory manuscript offers a process model based on second-order cybernetics, autopoietic systems theory and adaptive resilience frameworks. It employs three illustrative case vignettes – COVID-19 contact tracing in South Korea, California wildfire response and European flood management – to illustrate theoretical mechanisms before presenting a suggested validation framework with operationalized constructs. Findings We suggest that cybernetic resilience arises through three recursive mechanisms: (1) multi-level observation loops enabling systemic self-awareness, (2) structural couplings between human cognition and AI algorithms giving rise to hybrid cognitive capacities and (3) distributed coordination patterns yielding collective intelligence beyond the capability of individual agents. Originality/value This paper provides unique contributions. First, it reconceptualizes resilience as a dynamic recursive process and not as a static system property to overcome the limitations of both engineering and ecological models of resilience in human–AI systems. Second, socio-technical systems theory is extended by theorizing how hybrid human–AI configurations create emergent intelligence through unique structural-coupling mechanisms atypical from traditional human–technology interfaces.

items.title: Data and Algorithms: Strategic Disclosure of Competitiveness on Platforms Through Marketplace Analytics
items.abstract: This paper studies an e-commerce platform’s two intertwined decisions when offering marketplace analytics: the data access policy and the algorithm design. The data boom in e-commerce has spurred artificial intelligence (AI)-powered marketplace analytics, but platforms hold the data reins. Some adopt open data-access policies with third-party analytics providers (e.g., permitting data-scraping or application programming interface sharing), whereas others are restrictive. We ask why and when an e-commerce platform—capable of designing its own analytics to control sellers’ actions—may benefit from open data-access policies to accommodate competing third-party analytics services, despite the potential drawbacks of weakening its data advantages and control. We analyze two intertwined decisions an e-commerce platform can make when designing analytics to predict market competitiveness and assist sellers’ pricing decisions involving (1) data-access policy and (2) algorithm design. We find that platforms may use over-optimistic algorithms (by increasing the likelihood of generating low-competition signals) in their own analytics to boost commissions. Because sellers do not trust the platform to act in their best interest, they may be reluctant to adopt a platform’s analytics, resulting in a lose–lose situation and prompting the platform to allow data access to third-party providers. Overall, platforms gain from open data-access strategies in markets with moderately strong or weak competition. Finally, privacy legislation aimed at curtailing platforms’ data-sharing practices may inadvertently hurt consumers. History: Anthony Dukes served as the senior editor. items.abstract: Bài báo đề xuất khung phân tích học tập lấy tri thức làm trung tâm (Knowledge-Centered Learning Analytics Framework - KCLAF) - một khung bốn lớp nhằm giải quyết học tập phân mảnh (Fragmented Learning – FL) và quá tải nhận thức (Cognitive Overload – CL) trong học tập số. Dữ liệu từ 266 sinh viên Trường Đại học Mở Hà Nội (bảng hỏi Likert 5 mức, 57 mục, 11 cấu trúc) được phân tích bằng phân tích nhân tố khám phá (Exploratory Factor Analysis – EFA) và phân tích nhân tố khẳng định (Confirmatory Factor Analysis – CFA), hồi quy bình phương nhỏ nhất thông thường (Ordinary Least Squares – OLS) phân lớp với sai số chuẩn vững HC3 (heteroskedasticity-consistent, dạng 3) và phân tích trung gian bằng kỹ thuật lấy mẫu lặp. FL (M = 3,556) và CL (M = 3,597) cao hơn có ý nghĩa so với điểm giữa thang đo, với 30,5% và 36,1% sinh viên đạt mức từ 4,0 trở lên. Tổ chức tri thức (Knowledge Organizing – OR) là biến dự báo học sâu mạnh nhất (β = 0,348) và trung gian khoảng 44,9% liên hệ giữa sử dụng trí tuệ nhân tạo (Artificial Intelligence – AI) và học sâu (Deep Approach Learning – DL). Trái với giả thuyết ban đầu về nghịch lý AI–OR, hai biến tương quan dương (r = 0,458); tuy nhiên chỉ số khoảng cách chuẩn hóa giữa chúng ở cấp cá nhân có liên hệ nghịch với học sâu sau khi kiểm soát mức độ chung (β = −0,127; p = 0,046). Nghiên cứu ghi nhận hai hạn chế đo lường: năm cấu trúc kiến tạo tri thức không tách bạch được về thực nghiệm và thiên lệch đồng thuận. KCLAF được định vị là khung khái niệm cần kiểm chứng, kèm lộ trình bốn giai đoạn.

items.title: Decision-Support Ability of Large Language Models in Uncertain Environments: A Benchmark
items.abstract: As large language models increasingly take part in judgments about work, family, intimate relationships and other real-life problems, users' expectations have shifted from ``getting an answer'' to ``getting decision support.'' Unlike knowledge Q\&A, real-life problems typically involve incomplete information, limited perspectives, conflicting parties, uncertain risks and irreversible consequences. This paper proposes and tests a benchmark of decision-support ability in uncertain environments. We selected six large language models (GPT, Claude, DeepSeek, Doubao, Qwen, and ERNIE Bot) and had each answer six real-life scenarios in a separate window, in a single round. We analyzed the answers along several dimensions, including problem identification, information boundaries, risk calibration, degree of intervention, identification of the decision-making party, and action recommendations. The tests show that the differences between models lie not only in knowledge or reasoning ability, but in whether a model, facing uncertain information, realizes what it does not yet know, and controls its judgments, interventions and action recommendations accordingly. Models can generally recognize common risks and invoke corresponding solutions. But they also tend to enter ``problem-solving mode'' too early, get pulled into templates by risk keywords, narrow the space of possibilities too soon, misplace the decision-making party, or push irreversible actions when information is insufficient. We therefore argue that decision-support ability is not merely the ability to ``give a good plan,'' but the ability to ``know how far to go when one does not know all the facts.'' On this basis, we further propose a practical safe-response framework for higher-risk scenarios, to explore what large language models still need in order to move from ``being able to answer questions'' to ``truly helping people deal with real-world problems.''

items.title: Decoding systemic vascular health and hypertensive disorders in pregnancy through retinal imaging and Visionary AI
items.abstract: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy arise from early placental and systemic vascular dysfunction, yet current first-trimester screening remains imprecise, biologically opaque and logistically challenging. Here we present Visionary AI, an interpretable platform that integrates retinal imaging with graph-based vascular modeling to predict hypertensive disorders before clinical onset. Visionary AI converts retinal images into topological and geometric representations of microvascular structure, enabling risk prediction from biologically grounded vascular features rather than generic image embeddings or clinical variables. In a prospective development cohort of 1,267 pregnancies, Visionary AI achieved strong performance for preeclampsia across population-wide control settings (area under the curve (AUC) = 0.91, average precision (AP) = 0.81). A stability-optimized model transferred without retraining to an independent external validation cohort, achieving AUC = 0.81 and AP = 0.68 and outperforming clinical and deep learning benchmarks. Recurrent features involving retinal vascular topology, geometry, network complexity and hierarchical organization position the maternal retina as a minimally invasive biosensor of systemic vascular health and Visionary AI as a biologically interpretable framework for pregnancy risk stratification. An interpretable artificial intelligence framework predicts hypertensive disorders of pregnancy using retinal images and vascular modeling.

items.title: Deep learning
items.abstract: Deep learning is one of the most significant methods in modern artificial intelligence. Its power is that it is capable of automatically finding features and appreciating intricate patterns previously very hard to reproduce. The development of the field proceeded in stages: beginning with perceptron models of the mid-twentieth century, passing through moments of abandonment and resurgence, and more recently reaching some sorts of transformer architectures. On the way, it was necessary for the researchers to overcome challenges such as vanishing gradients and the enormous computational expediency of training big models. A breakthrough arrived in the 2010. Improved hardware, new training methods, and the availability of huge datasets enabled deep learning to take off in practical applications. Convolutional neural network reimagined computer vision and recurrent neural network along with long short-term memory networks enabled sequence modelling as in language and speech. Transformer models incorporating attention mechanisms reign in natural language processing as we speak constantly zeroing in on new records in performance. It is not only scalable but also malleable that makes deep learning unique. From finance and healthcare to autonomous systems, the impact is obvious. As the area continues to grow, it is bound to continue as a key player in the course of artificial intelligence.

items.title: Deep Learning for Medical Image Analysis: A Comprehensive Review
items.abstract: As deep learning continues to develop at a fast pace, the field of medical imaging has also seen significant changes due to new technologies making it possible to automatically analyse large amounts of complex image data with much greater accuracy and efficiency than ever before. In this chapter, we will describe and examine many different deep-teaching techniques used in various imaging modalities such as MRI (Magnetic Resonance Imaging), CT (Computed Tomography), X-ray, Ultrasound, Mammograms, and Dermatoscopic as well as Digital Pathology images. We will also discuss several key deep-teaching architectures including CNN (Convolutional Neural Networks), ViT (Vision Transformer), and GAN (Generative Adversarial Networks), and how these architectures can be used in the performance of standard imaging tasks including Image Classification, Object Detection, Image Segmentation, and Image Registration. Moving forward, from the years 2023 through 2025 there will be greater use of Foundation Models, Multimodal Large Language Models, Diffusion-based Data Generation, Real-time Surgical AI, Explainable Transformers, and Federated Learning for training with Privacy Assurance. Finally, we will provide insight into potential future areas for research including Developing Universal Vision-Language Models, AI-driven Precision Medicine, Developing Generalizable Algorithms, Integration into Clinical Settings, and the Importance of Human-AI Collaboration.

items.title: Deep Learning for Personalized Medicine and Precision Healthcare
items.abstract: The combination of artificial intelligence (AI) and precision medicine could potentially change the way medicine is practiced. In this scenario, advances in precision medicine technology will enable healthcare providers to identify the phenotype of each patient who has a unique β-cell response to treatment, as well as other clinical requirements related to their disease. Using AI, sophisticated computers and techniques can help generate insights and create intelligent systems, thereby giving increased decision-making abilities to healthcare professionals. The latest scientific literature shows that as translational research into this combination of precision medicine and AI becomes more widespread, many of the challenges of implementing precision medicine might be addressed. Specifically, this means considering nongenomic, as well as genomic, factors; patient symptoms; clinical history; and lifestyle data in the complete evaluation and management of each patient, which will provide greater diagnostic accuracy and prognostic ability. One of the important causes of diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a common complication of diabetes and has affected many millions of people with diabetes throughout the world. DR, like many complications of diabetes is progressive and typically goes undetected until it reaches a stage of nonpreventable blindness. This chapter describes an investigation of the implementation of state-of-the-art deep learning methods in the detection and classification of diabetic retinopathy (DR). This chapter ends with some promising further research topics, including explainable artificial intelligence (AI) to strengthen trust as a mechanism, federated learning as a mechanism to facilitate data privacy, and edge AI as a mechanism to implement rapid on-site screening in underserved healthcare domains.

items.title: Deep Learning Methods for Cardiovascular Disease Detection in CT and MRI Scans
items.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain a leading health concern worldwide and increase the demand for rapid and accurate diagnostic techniques. Although CT and MRI imaging provide excellent cardiac studies, most analysis is slow and inconsistent when performed manually. Deep learning techniques showed strong potential in providing automated interpretation of images, improving accuracy in segmentation, and enabling the classification of diseases reliably. This review recapitulates recent deep learning approaches using CT and MRI for the detection of CVD: CNN-based, hybrid, and transformer-driven models. It examines the primary barriers to using deep learning methods in cardiovascular medical imaging, including limited access to annotated datasets, transparency of models, and the ability to apply findings from one center to another. The Similarly, the paper proposes several novel approaches for addressing these barriers including federated learning, multi-modal fusion in DL models as well as explainable artificial intelligence. These approaches may greatly facilitate the transition of DL technologies into clinics.

items.title: Defending against deepfake speech attacks via feature dropout and dropin regularization in large audio language models
items.abstract: Deepfakes have raised widespread concern owing to their threats to privacy, security, and societal trust, driving growing research interest in effective detection methods. Audio deepfake detection has moved from handcrafted-feature classifiers to end-to-end deep learning architectures and, more recently, to self-supervised speech foundation models and general-purpose speech recognizers such as Whisper. The use of instruction-following speech large language models (LLMs), of which Speech Audio Language Music Open Neural Network (SALMONN) is a representative example, remains comparatively less explored, and forms the setting of this study. We argue that large language models (LLMs), with their powerful representational and information retrieval capabilities, hold significant potential for this task—provided that relevant audio features are carefully selected and prioritized. To this end, we employ a speech LLM, specifically SALMONN, for deepfake audio detection, incorporating a two-stage training strategy in which Stage 1 injects acoustic-feature awareness into the Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) adapters via an auxiliary feature-prediction pretext task (referred to as feature dropin), and Stage 2 performs windowed random retention on the encoder token sequence (referred to as feature dropout) before the final real/fake decision. Our approach achieves an absolute accuracy improvement of 0.188 on the FakeOrReal benchmark and attains state-of-the-art performance on the Automatic Speaker Verification Spoofing and Countermeasures (ASVspoof) 2019 LA subset with an Equal Error Rate (EER) of 0.00496, representing a 33.0% relative improvement over prior methods. Furthermore, the model transfers non-trivially to an out-of-domain artificial intelligence (AI)-generated music dataset (M6), reaching accuracy comparable to a ResNet18 baseline reported in prior study, which we interpret as evidence of transferable audio representations rather than broad cross-domain robustness.

items.title: Deliverable No D3.5 Production Planning & Reconfiguration v1
items.abstract: Deliverable D3.5 Production Planning & Reconfiguration v1 provides an overall status update of two core components developed within the CIRCMAN5.0 project’s Work Package 3 (WP3). They are aligned with WP3’s purpose that is to deliver novel simulation and modelling software to improve process and product manufacturing. The first component corresponds to task T3.4 titled “ML-Assisted Production Planning”, is led by ICCS and is dedicated to the development of Machine Learning (ML) algorithms that support the production planning and resource allocation. The second component corresponds to subtask T3.4.1 titled “Embedded edge computing system for the automatic detection of multi-type defects”, is led by CERTH and is dedicated to the automatic detection of multi-type defects in silicon photovoltaic (PV) modules through the design and development of an on-line embedded Internet of Things (IoT) edge computing system. In this first version of D3.5, the challenges and opportunities associated with the transition towards Industry 5.0 (I5.0) are analysed. items.title: Demography and Adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Nigerian Higher Institutions: Implication on the Needs for Policy Implementation
items.abstract: Demography plays a crucial role in understanding the adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Nigerian Higher institutions as different demographic factor can influence the rate and extent of the adoption. This paper analyzed Demography and adoption of AI in Nigerian Higher institutions with the focus of examining the factors influencing the adoption of Artificial Intelligence in Nigerian Higher Institutions and the needs for policy on its adoption. The paper relied on secondary sources of data such as documented Journals, articles and books written in the area of Demography and adoption of AI in Nigerian higher institution for its analyses. Drawing from the Social Learning Theory the article argued that graduate students' self-efficacy is correlated with their beliefs about their capacity to use and benefit from AI-powered technologies, and outcome expectations are correlated with their beliefs about the possible consequences and outcomes of using AI. Findings suggest that AI adoption in Nigerian Higher institutions is still in its early stage, with many participants recognizing both the potential benefits and the challenges associated with AI integration. More importantly, interactions with artificial intelligence (AI)-based educational tools might be influenced by various demographic factors, including age, gender, marital status, prior technology experience, learning preferences, the type of academic programs, level of education, urban / rural location of the institutions, and socio-economic status of students. The paper recommends among others that policy makers and educators should address potential disparities and ensure equitable access to AI education considering factors like age, gender, location of the institution and socio-economic status in order for Nigerian to prepare its students for the digital age and foster economic growth and development.

items.title: Design and preliminary psychometric validation of an ergonomics-oriented questionnaire applied to mexican teleworkers in working from home conditions using exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses
items.abstract: This paper develops and psychometrically validates a four-factor WFH ergonomics questionnaire and examines its factorial validity and reliability in Mexican teleworkers. WFH studies have gained global attention, yet research linking WFH environments to musculoskeletal discomfort remains limited in Mexico. To address this gap, the questionnaire was developed through comprehensive literature review and digitally distributed to N=202 Mexican teleworkers in the manufacturing sector. The questionnaire was preliminary validated through EFA & CFA analyses using factor loadings for item selection and Scree plot, Eigenvalue and Parallel analysis for factor selection to obtain a refined 12-variable and 4-factor model. Statistical validation involved goodness of fit indices, internal consistency and reliability, and convergent and discriminant validity. Because the CFA was conducted on a non-independent sample, the model fit results may therefore be optimistic. The questionnaire provides a standardized basis for ergonomic risk surveillance among teleworkers, supporting preventive interventions at organizational and national levels.

items.title: Designing an AI-Responsive Early Childhood Curriculum: A Conceptual Framework for Supporting Developmental Learning Trajectories in Preschool Education
items.abstract: Background The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and deep learning technologies into education creates new opportunities for personalized learning in early childhood education (ECE). Yet limited research has examined how educators interpret and enact AI-responsive curriculum decisions in preschool settings, particularly in culturally diverse contexts. Purpose This study explores educators’ experiences in designing and implementing AI-responsive curricula and develops a conceptual framework explaining how AI can inform curriculum decision-making for young children without displacing teacher judgment. Method An interpretive phenomenological study was conducted at TK Harapan Bangsa, Makassar, Indonesia, with nine adult participants: six preschool teachers, two curriculum specialists, and one AI tool developer-collaborator whose expert interview supplied technical context. Data comprised two in-depth interviews with each teacher, interviews with curriculum specialists and the developer-collaborator, 18 non-participant observations, and analysis of AI-supported planning documents. MAXQDA 2024 supported data management. Giorgi’s phenomenological method was operationalized through first-order meaning units, second-order interpretive themes, and third-order composite constructs. Triangulation, reflexive memoing, an audit trail, member checking, and peer debriefing supported trustworthiness. Findings Three interconnected constructs emerged. Predictive Developmental Tracking describes AI-supported identification of developmental readiness and possible concerns. AI-Responsive Curriculum Adaptation captures teachers’ active interrogation and contextual modification of algorithmic recommendations. Deep Learning as Pedagogical Scaffold positions AI as a support that amplifies, rather than replaces, professional expertise. Together, the constructs informed the AI-Responsive Curriculum Design (ARCD) Framework. Conclusion The ARCD Framework explains AI-responsive curriculum implementation as a relational process combining predictive insight, ecological sensitivity, and educator agency. It offers implications for curriculum policy, teacher professional development, and ethical AI integration in ECE.

items.title: Development and Validation of the Effectiveness of a Global Occupational Health and Safety Management System Model for Japanese Companies
items.abstract: Abstract Objectives To extend a Global Occupational Health and Safety Management System Model for Japanese companies—a hybrid model integrating the ISO 45001 standard with company-wide minimum standards set by headquarters and good practices adapted to local conditions—beyond Southeast Asia, the region covered in the original pilot study, and to verify its long-term effectiveness. Methods At a large Japanese manufacturer of construction and mining machinery, we examined, over 2013-2026 (a net 12 years, excluding a 2-year suspension during the COVID-19 pandemic): the development of headquarters functions, and changes in 13 performance-audit item scores at 8 production sites in North America, Europe, and Asia. Results All 9 headquarters functions were established over approximately 12 years. Total audit scores increased at 6 of the 8 production sites; 2 sites showed no improvement. The largest numbers of sites remained below the target level for risk-reduction measures and risk assessment; together with officer competency, the only item showing no change in mean score, these findings revealed a structural lag in occupational hygiene relative to safety. Conclusions The model promoted both headquarters maturation and site-level improvement outside Southeast Asia. Strengthening occupational hygiene will require more direct headquarters interventions, such as expert dispatch and technical support, in addition to standard-setting and auditing.

items.title: Development of natural gas quality tracking technology: From steady-state simulation to intelligent hybrid modeling
items.abstract: With the creation of China’s National Integrated Pipeline Network and the transition to natural gas energy measurement, quality fluctuations caused by multisource gas mixing pose severe challenges to trade fairness and pipeline network safety. As a key technology for achieving accurate energy measurement, natural gas quality tracking has undergone a paradigm shift: from steady-state hydraulic calculations to transient composition tracking, and then to intelligent modeling paradigms that feature mechanism-data-driven collaboration. Through a systematic review of technological developments and an analysis of core algorithms, this paper highlights the core value of this technology, namely, its ability to significantly reduce reliance on online gas chromatographs, thereby providing a technical solution to promote energy measurement at Class B and C station yards. It further explores the new challenges presented by hydrogen-blended natural gas and other novel gas sources, including property calculations, numerical dissipation, and safety assessments. Ultimately, future research on this technology should focus on the deep integration of mechanistic models and artificial intelligence, propelling quality-tracking technology toward high precision, strong real-time capabilities, and wide adaptability. This review aims to provide a theoretical reference and technical support for the development of China’s self-sufficient, controllable natural gas energy measurement system.

items.title: Development of Oral English Production Through Artificial Intelligence Tools in Eight Grade Students at Unidad Educativa Fiscal Bicentenario D7
items.abstract: Modern society is undergoing rapid educational changes driven by technological evolution and rising academic demands, establishing Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Information and Communication Technologies (ICT) as key tools for teaching English as a Foreign Language (EFL). This study evaluates the use of AI tools to enhance oral production (speaking skills) among 107 eighth-grade students (sections A, B, and C) at the *Unidad Educativa Fiscal Bicentenario D7 Vespertino* in Quito, Ecuador. The methodology employed a quantitative, descriptive field study design. Key diagnostic findings reveal that 73% of students struggle with initial oral fluency, and 75% report frequent pronunciation errors. However, 68% state that practicing with AI tools boosts their confidence and significantly reduces communication anxiety when speaking in public. Furthermore, 70% demonstrate high motivation for learning through technological resources. Critical limitations identified include limited instructional time (three hours per week), a lack of independent practice outside the classroom (75%), and recurring connectivity and infrastructure issues (56%). The study concludes that overcoming these barriers and the digital divide requires the design and implementation of low-data adaptive micro-learning modules, independent practice guides, and continuous teacher training workshops.

items.title: Development of RAG-Based Generative AI Application: Application of Generative AI in RAG-Based Web Development
items.abstract: Abstract The rapid evolution of Generative Artificial Intelligence (Generative AI) and Large Language Models (LLMs) has transformed the landscape of intelligent web application development. Despite their remarkable fluency, standalone LLMs frequently suffer from hallucination, outdated knowledge, and an inability to reference verifiable, domain-specific information, which limits their reliability in enterprise contexts. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) addresses these limitations by coupling a parametric language model with a non-parametric retrieval mechanism that fetches relevant information from an external knowledge base at inference time. This paper presents the design, methodology, and prototype architecture of a RAG-based generative AI web application intended to demonstrate how retrieval, semantic search, and prompt engineering can be combined with modern web development practices to build context-aware, factually grounded AI systems. The proposed system integrates a document ingestion and chunking pipeline, sentence-level embedding generation, a vector database for high-dimensional semantic search, and a large language model layer responsible for grounded response generation. The web application is designed using a React.js/Next.js frontend, a FastAPI/Node.js backend, JWT-based authentication, and a cloud-native deployment strategy using Docker, Kubernetes, and CI/CD pipelines on platforms such as AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud Platform. The paper reviews recent literature on RAG architectures, compares leading vector databases (Pinecone, FAISS, ChromaDB, Milvus) and embedding models, and surveys contributions from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, Meta AI, Microsoft Research, Hugging Face, LangChain, and LlamaIndex. Rather than reporting fabricated experimental numbers, this work proposes a rigorous evaluation methodology — covering retrieval accuracy, groundedness, latency, and user satisfaction — that can be applied once the prototype is fully deployed. The study concludes that RAG-based architectures offer a practical, scalable, and enterprise-ready pathway toward building trustworthy generative AI web applications, while identifying open challenges such as embedding quality, context-window constraints, and operational cost that motivate future work in agentic and multimodal RAG systems. Keywords: Generative AI, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), Large Language Models (LLMs), Prompt Engineering, Vector Database, Semantic Search, AI Chatbot, Web Development, Cloud Deployment, Enterprise Applications.

items.title: Differentiating linked cognitive states under task demand and sleep restriction: toward an experimental framework for operational monitoring
items.abstract: Real-world settings involve multiple interacting cognitive states such as mental workload, drowsiness, fatigue, and mind wandering, yet these are typically studied in isolation. A critical question is whether these states can be empirically differentiated given that they share overlapping behavioral and physiological signatures. We investigated whether task difficulty and sleep restriction produce dissociable effects across these states, and whether their response patterns reflect distinct underlying mechanisms or a common cognitive resource using a unified framework. Participants from operational populations (Study 1: n = 40; Study 2: n = 27) performed three complementary tasks (MATB-II, N-Back, and SART) under two manipulations: task difficulty and partial sleep restriction, targeting cognitive load and alertness. Increasing task difficulty degraded performance and increased perceived workload and fatigue across tasks. In contrast, sleep restriction primarily elevated subjective drowsiness and mind wandering, with smaller, task-dependent effects on performance. These findings provide evidence that cognitive and physiological states influencing situational awareness can be differentiated using complementary manipulations and characterized through distinct behavioral and subjective measures. This distinction provides a foundation for future predictive and monitoring approaches in applied settings.

items.title: Digital communication and occupational well-being in 25 European countries
items.abstract: Abstract This paper examines the association between digital communication at work and employee well-being, moderated by occupational status and the fulfillment of basic psychological needs. Two studies were conducted to investigate these relationships. Study 1 utilized data from the European Social Survey, encompassing 25 countries ( N = 24,331). Study 2 involved a longitudinal survey of Finnish workers ( N = 1817) collected at nine time points over 6-month intervals from 2019 to 2023. Multilevel regression models were employed to analyze the data. Study 1 found that digital communication positively correlates with job satisfaction in Europe, with a stronger effect observed among lower-position workers. Study 2 revealed that the use of digital platforms was associated with higher work engagement and women reported significantly higher work engagement than men. However, for higher-position office workers, particularly those in supervisory roles, increased use of organizational social media platforms and excessive social media use were linked to decreased work engagement. Several interaction effects indicated that the association between digital communication as well as digital tool use and work engagement and job satisfaction is contingent on basic psychological need satisfaction and occupational status. Organizations should tailor their digital communication strategies to account for employees’ occupational status and work autonomy. This paper addresses a gap in cross-national and longitudinal research on the impact of digital communication on workplace well-being. It provides insights into how digital communication tools differentially affect employees based on their occupational status and psychological needs.

items.title: Digital Marketing and Communication Strategies
items.abstract: This chapter examines digital communication, marketing, and institutional identity in higher education as interconnected organisational domains. It treats digitalisation as the foundation of institutional practice and digital communication as a managerial rather than purely promotional function. Institutional communication is analysed as an integrated process encompassing both external stakeholder engagement and internal communication. The chapter reviews the core platforms that underpin institutional communication, including websites, social media, email, and internal collaboration systems. It argues that strategic effectiveness depends less on the number of channels used than on their governance as a coherent, audience-centred portfolio. It also explores the role of Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs), podcasts, and EdTech tools, which increasingly combine communication, service delivery, and data generation. The chapter further considers how artificial intelligence is reshaping higher education marketing through personalisation, predictive analytics, and customer relationship management (CRM-)based engagement, while highlighting the importance of trust, transparency, and regulatory compliance. Finally, it argues that successful implementation depends on digital leadership, effective governance, capability development, and staff well-being, all of which shape whether digital transformation strengthens or weakens institutional coherence.

items.title: Digital Research Ecosystems
items.abstract: Digital research ecosystems (DREs) constitute the infrastructure core of contemporary academic scholarship, significantly altering how scientific knowledge is generated, organised, validated, and preserved. This comprehensive academic work provides an exhaustive, multi-layered analysis of DREs as integrated sociotechnical systems operating at the intersection of computational advancement and institutional evolution. It examines the historical shift towards data-intensive science, maps the emergence of the fourth paradigm of discovery, and investigates how these ecosystems support the lifecycle of research data through the operationalisation of open science principles. The structural components of DREs are dissected across multiple layers, emphasising the transformative role of artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, and automated knowledge systems in semantic discovery and automated curation. Furthermore, the analysis addresses critical systemic challenges, including technological fragmentation, academic capitalism, data silos, geopolitical digital inequalities, and the delicate ethical-legal tensions surrounding data privacy, surveillance, and security. Finally, it outlines emerging revolutionary paradigms such as Decentralised Science (DeSci) and autonomous, closed-loop research infrastructure, providing a robust theoretical framework for understanding the long-term trajectory of global scientific collaboration.

items.title: Digital transformation, technological innovation, and e-sports: ISSF at a new stage of shooting sport development
items.abstract: In the modern era, the survival of traditional sports disciplines is directly linked to their ability to adapt to a dynamic media environment. The International Shooting Sport Federation (ISSF) has entered a period of fundamental transformation, shifting from a closed technical discipline toward a high-demand global media product. The central challenge lies in changing the "cognitive perception" of shooting – transforming a process that appears static to an outside observer into an emotionally resonant and technologically accessible spectacle. This article analyzes the key directions of this process. First, it examines the diversification of content delivery through the aggressive scaling of digital presence and the exploration of new platforms. A vital aspect is the technological verification and increased transparency of officiating, achieved through the implementation of VAR objective control systems and "live aiming" shot visualization technologies. The study also investigates the integration of virtual reality and esports as a means of creating alternative "entry points" into the sport via digital simulators. Alongside these developments, the work analyses the associated risks and institutional consequences of this transformation. The implementation of innovations such as AI-driven hit analysis and VR tools fosters the necessary "immersive connection" between the athlete and the fan. This is critical for attracting sponsorship capital, as it allows dry technical data to be converted into engaging content. The findings are based on a comparative analysis of Redtorch reports (SportOnSocial 2025), official ISSF press releases, and current industry publications. items.title: Disciplinary Perspectives on the Relevance of AI Research Assistants for Scholarly Article Discovery
items.abstract: This study explored artificial intelligence (AI) research assistants through the lens of scholars from different disciplines as they interacted with the tools. The goal was to determine whether AI tools provide relevant scholarly literature or prioritize surface-level relevance at the expense of disciplinary depth, and to examine how scholars perceive the usefulness of the tools in teaching and learning. The study used a multiple-phase, qualitative design in which ten scholars from several disciplines completed structured search tasks in each AI research assistant (Consensus, Elicit, SciSpace), followed by semi-structured interviews. Data were analyzed using qualitative coding techniques, with themes developed through thematic analysis approach. Analysis involved data familiarization, memoing, iterative first and second cycle coding, and the generation and refinement of themes. The findings revealed six themes from the search task diaries and interviews with participants: article coverage varied across disciplines; discipline specific information needs and resource mismatch; a complementary resource for scholarly article discovery; AI summaries technically correct but generic; faculty perceptions on AI tools in student learning; usability and cognitive load considerations. The findings indicate that while most tools surfaced additional research from scholarly journals, they often did not consistently identify seminal literature across the sampled disciplines. AI summaries on the literature were perceived as factually correct but generic. Lastly, participants expressed varied perceptions about the ways in which the tools could be used in teaching and learning contexts.

items.title: Dissecting AI discourse
items.abstract: Abstract This study investigates the discourse characteristics of AI-generated argumentative essays designed to simulate student writing, comparing them with human-authored texts to explore linguistic variation and its implications for academic discourse. While large language models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT demonstrate impressive fluency and coherence, questions remain about their capacity to engage in nuanced argumentation and the critical reasoning expected in academic contexts. Employing Biber’s (1988) multidimensional (MD) analysis, this study examines systematic differences between LLM-generated and human-written essays across dimensions of register variation, informational density, syntactic complexity, and persuasion. The results reveal that ChatGPT essays are markedly more informationally dense, context-independent, and abstract, yet exhibit reduced interpersonal engagement and overt persuasion compared with student essays. The paper concludes by reflecting on broader pedagogical and ethical implications for the integration of AI tools into academic writing and corpus-based research.

items.title: Driver Responses to Mismatches Between Expected and Experienced Automated Vehicle Driving Styles
items.abstract: Automated vehicles (AV) can exhibit diverse driving behaviors that deviate from driver expectations. More research is needed to understand drivers’ preferred driving styles when navigating safety-critical situations as well as their responses to unexpected AV driving behaviors. Forty-eight participants experienced simulated automated driving scenarios where an AV navigated a construction zone while exhibiting four different predefined driving styles that varied in terms of cautiousness and efficiency. After each trial, participants provided feedback to adjust the AV’s driving style toward their preferences, which was successfully implemented in 80% cases. Drivers’ trust, workload, voluntary takeover decisions, eye movements, and skin conductance were measured. Overall, participants preferred driving styles balancing cautiousness and efficiency. When AV behavior matched driver preferences, they reported higher trust and more stable visual scanning patterns, while unexpected behaviors were associated with broader ocular scanning. Findings can inform the development of adaptive systems that intelligently modify AV behaviors.
